ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Unexpected respiratory depression

A patient takes a codeine-containing cough medicine at the prescribed dose and develops marked sedation with slow breathing. Genetic testing later identifies unusually rapid CYP2D6 activity. Which metabolic change best explains the excessive opioid effect?

  1. Accelerated conversion of codeine to morphine
  2. Failure to convert morphine to codeine
  3. Enhanced renal elimination of morphine
  4. Reduced absorption of oral codeine
  5. Increased inactivation of opioid receptors
Answer and explanation

Accelerated conversion of codeine to morphine

CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolism can generate high morphine exposure.

Option explanations

Accelerated conversion of codeine to morphine: CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolism can generate high morphine exposure.

Failure to convert morphine to codeine: The clinically relevant conversion proceeds from codeine to morphine.

Enhanced renal elimination of morphine: Faster elimination would generally lower opioid exposure.

Reduced absorption of oral codeine: Reduced absorption would decrease rather than intensify effects.

Increased inactivation of opioid receptors: Receptor inactivation would reduce responsiveness.
